notes.title: Chapter 2 source scope and exercise count
notes.content: Chapter 2 of B.B. Agarwal, S.P. Tayal, and M. Gupta (2010), Software Engineering & Testing: An Introduction, spans printed pp. 29–52. Its 20 written exercises are on printed p. 52. Classify the main requested action as 14 explain/list/define/describe, 3 compare/evaluate, 1 model selection exercise with four scenario subparts, 2 explicit diagram tasks; Q8 also has a diagram as a secondary action. No calculations in this set. These are item-count shares, not exam marks.

notes.title: Current depth and source-war rule (student clarification 2026-10-16)
notes.content: The professor supplies vocabulary rather than a full lecture account. Treat his exact vocabulary list as the chapter scope when received. For each term, explain enough to understand the definition, mechanism, conditions, distinctions, and any required diagram, with modest added depth to repair gaps in slides. Do not produce an exhaustive survey or add every model from every textbook. Compare sources term by term: use the course-aligned book where adequate; bring in one strongest supporting source only when the primary/slide coverage is absent or materially weaker/unclear; cite the source and page. A source-war is selective gap-filling, not a merge of all books.

notes.title: Professor-pattern evidence and limits (student-supplied 5-word.json)
notes.content: The supplied OpenCode history “5-word.json” records the student’s previous method: take a professor vocabulary list, map its terms against the relevant Aggarwal/Singh slides and books, determine whether the source fully covers each term, then research only uncovered items. The student later clarified that this is pattern evidence from prior Design/Metrics work, not a claim that the professor gave Chapter 2 vocabulary or that all Chapter 5/6 content belongs to Chapter 2. The present Chapter 2 vocabulary remains unconfirmed.
